im-c58-01.h: 단순 가정 (-(으)면) vs 필수 전제 조건 (-아/어야)

a.d: Sets up a neutral possibility or habitual trigger; other options may still exist.
ex: 시간이 **있으면** 책을 읽어요. — If I have time, I read books.

b.d: Sets up an indispensable requirement; without it, the outcome is completely impossible.
ex: 유효한 여권이 **있어야** 비행기에 탑승할 수 있어요. — Only by having a valid passport can you board the airplane.

im-c58-01.tip: -아/어야 is frequently followed by can/cannot expressions (-(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다) or essential results (비로소 알다).

im-c58-01.q: Fix the sentence where a strict legal requirement was improperly formed with an unnatural ending.
im-c58-01.wrong: 만 18세 이상이 되거든 운전면허 시험에 응시할 수 있어요.
answers: 만 18세 이상이 되어야 운전면허 시험에 응시할 수 있어요.
만 18세 이상이 되어야 운전면허 시험에 응시할 수 있어요
만 18세 이상이 되어야만 운전면허 시험에 응시할 수 있어요.
만 18세 이상이 되어야만 운전면허 시험에 응시할 수 있어요
im-c58-01.hint: Use the indispensable requirement ending -아/어야: 되어야.
im-c58-01.why: Age requirements are mandatory prerequisites, demanding -아/어야 rather than -거든.

ko: 해외로 여행을 떠나려면 반드시 유효한 여권이 있어야 합니다.
일부 국가의 경우 입국 비자를 사전에 미리 발급받아야 비행기에 탑승할 수 있습니다.

en: To leave for overseas travel, you must have a valid passport without fail.

im-c58-01.q: What is an indispensable condition to board flights to certain foreign destinations?

im-c58-01.q: What grammatical meaning does -아/어야 convey across the passage?
options: A mandatory prerequisite without which following results cannot be accomplished
A past event that was unexpectedly interrupted
A casual hypothetical joke
im-c58-01.why: -아/어야 marks an indispensable condition necessary for the subsequent action.

im-c58-02.h: 연결 어미 (-거든 가정·지시) vs 종결 어미 (-거든요 이유)

a.d: Connects two clauses: if condition A happens in the future, follow through with instruction/promise B.
ex: 집에 **도착하거든** 바로 손부터 씻어라. — When you arrive home, wash your hands right away.

b.d: Placed at the very end of a statement to gently provide background context or reasons to the listener.
ex: 오늘은 일찍 잘 거예요. 내일 일찍 **일어나야 하거든요**. — I will sleep early today, because I have to wake up early tomorrow.

im-c58-02.tip: Clause connector -거든 is strictly followed by imperative (명령), propositive (청유), or promissory (약속) sentences, not plain factual statements.

im-c58-02.q: Fix the sentence where -거든 was inappropriately paired with a past tense factual sentence instead of an instruction.
im-c58-02.wrong: 서울에 놀러 오시거든 어제 남산타워에 갔어요.
answers: 서울에 놀러 오시거든 저희 집에 꼭 들르세요.
서울에 놀러 오시거든 저희 집에 꼭 들르세요
서울에 놀러 오시거든 연락해 주세요.
서울에 놀러 오시거든 연락해 주세요
im-c58-02.hint: -거든 requires an imperative or invitation in the following clause: 들르세요 / 연락해 주세요.
im-c58-02.why: -거든 must be followed by a directive, suggestion, or promise regarding future circumstances.

items.ex: 문제가 잘 해결되거든 소식 전해 주세요.

im-c58-02.q: What does the passage suggest if the reader visits Insadong?

im-c58-02.q: What grammatical clause types typically follow the connector -거든?
options: Commands, suggestions, or promises (명령 · 청유 · 약속)
Past tense factual descriptions
Historical textbook chronologies
im-c58-02.why: -거든 pairs with imperatives, propositives, and promises for anticipated situations.

items: I can set up conditional requests and invitations using connecting -거든.

a.d: Designates the one indispensable prerequisite without which the result is barred.
ex: 비자를 **받아야** 출국할 수 있어요. — Only by receiving a visa can you leave the country.

b.d: Sets a future trigger situation immediately followed by an action directive or promise.
ex: 퇴근**하거든** 시원한 맥주 한잔하자. — When you get off work, let’s have a cold beer.

im-c58-03.tip: -(으)면 is general hypothesis without clause restrictions. -아/어야 stresses necessity. -거든 specifically anticipates an event and gives instructions.

im-c58-03.q: Which conditional ending is used to specify the strict requirement for opening an account?

im-c58-03.q: Why is -거든 used in the last sentence of the passage?

im-c58-03.why: -거든 sets up an upcoming trigger followed by an advisory reminder (챙기세요).

items: I can pick accurately between -(으)면, -아/어야, and -거든 depending on clause requirements.
I can express strict procedural conditions and timely behavioral instructions effortlessly.

a.d: States non-negotiable operational requirements, laws, and institutional standards.
ex: 소방 시설 점검을 **통과해야** 영업 허가가 나옵니다. — Only by passing fire facility inspection will a business license be issued.

b.d: Invites cooperation or actions triggered by upcoming events.
ex: 회의 자료가 **완성되거든** 팀장님께 먼저 보고해 주세요. — When meeting materials are completed, please report to the team lead first.

im-c58-04.tip: In official customer service, use -아/어야 for mandatory requirements, and -거든 for courteous situational guidance.
